newsitem.title: FRANCE: Dassault wants strong dollar - paper.
newsitem.headline: Dassault wants strong dollar - paper.

text.p: The chairman of French aircraft maker Dassault Aviation said on Sunday he wanted a strong dollar and a change in the franc/mark parity.
"The strong franc policy has been he followed since (former prime minister Pierre) Beregovoy and that is a pity," Serge Dassault said in an interview with Sunday newspaper Journal de Dimanche.
Beregovoy served as prime minister in 1992-93.
"I want a strong dollar. The Americans are not doing anything in this direction. So it is left to changing the franc/mark parity," he said.
French aerospace firms, including state-owned Aerospatiale, are penalised as U.S. rivals benefit from a weaker currency in a world market where sales are made in dollars.
French company costs are also, naturally, incurred in the stronger franc currency.

"The British had the intelligence to devalue their currency and what is more, they have lower payroll costs than we do," Dassault said. "They come out ahead because their production costs are lower than ours."
Dassault and Aerospatiale are in merger talks as part of the French government's attempts to consolidate the defence industry.
